title: 17 U.S.C. § 1201 — Circumvention of copyright protection systems (incl. § 1201(f) interoperability exception)
key_finding: Anti-circumvention liability attaches independently of infringement; § 1201(f) is a narrow interoperability exception for RE — defeating obfuscation/anti-tamper on a venue client carries § 1201 exposure.

title: 37 CFR § 201.40 — Exemptions to prohibition against circumvention (Librarian of Congress triennial rulemaking)
key_finding: Conditional exemptions exist (e.g., limited security-research classes); RE outside the enumerated classes is not excused.

title: Directive 2009/24/EC on the legal protection of computer programs (codified)
key_finding: Art. 5: lawful user may observe/study/test functioning during entitled use; Art. 6: decompilation only if indispensable for interoperability, info not otherwise readily available, limited to necessary parts, no substantially-similar program — documented venue APIs defeat the Art. 6 precondition.

title: Directive (EU) 2016/943 — trade secrets protection
key_finding: Recital 16/Art. 3(1)(b): know-how from reverse engineering a lawfully acquired product is lawful acquisition; the Directive targets theft/breach, but studying leaked code is unlawful acquisition with downstream liability.

title: hiQ Labs, Inc. v. LinkedIn Corp., No. 17-16783 (9th Cir. 2022, on remand)
key_finding: After Van Buren, scraping publicly available website data falls outside CFAA even post-cease-and-desist; protection covers public data only — auth-protected endpoints and off-limits system parts remain CFAA territory.

title: Computer Associates Int'l, Inc. v. Altai, Inc., 982 F.2d 693 (2d Cir. 1992)
key_finding: Abstraction–filtration–comparison test; court endorsed clean-room development (spec-only wall, independent implementation) as the defensible procedure for building behaviorally similar software.

title: Page MJ et al., The PRISMA 2020 statement (BMJ 2021;372:n71)
key_finding: 27-item systematic-review reporting checklist — the template for formalizing this repo's evidence sweeps (protocol, search log, inclusion criteria, evidence table, dated synthesis).

title: GRADE Working Group — overview of the GRADE approach
key_finding: Four certainty tiers (high/moderate/low/very low) with explicit downgrade criteria — maps onto the repo's [verified]/[INFERENCE] discipline as a three-tier confidence tag.

title: Ghidra — NSA open-source disassembler/decompiler
key_finding: No lawful closed target with value for the five named systems: CBB/TierZero/NeuralArb are server-side desks with no client binary; open repos need no RE.

title: mitmproxy — HTTPS interception proxy
key_finding: Defensible only for intercepting traffic you are authorized to generate (own account, own client); venue-client instrumentation is EULA-encumbered.

title: XEMM — Rust maker/taker two-leg bot (Pacifica↔Hyperliquid)
key_finding: Open source: maker price derived from taker hedge price, 4-layer deduped fill detection, hedge queue 256 with halt-on-overflow, ±3 bps profit-deviation cancel — read the code, no RE needed.

title: counterfactual5/funding-arb (MIT)
key_finding: Live-tested Lighter + OKX venue adapters, cross-venue executor with rollback, settle-mismatch planner — procurement candidate for the execution 80%.

title: alexanderlmoran/funding-arb-bot risks.md
key_finding: Open documentation of kill-switch hierarchy, partial-fill retry (3×/60s then flatten), data-freshness veto (>2 min stale = no trade) — published risk rules, nothing to reverse.

title: CBB equity-perps arb writeup (X article, via hyperindex mirror)
key_finding: Closed desk but self-published mechanism + parameters (maxDelta 800, cancelDelta 0.02, takerRatio 0.05/0.10) + $1.1m stale-feed postmortem — the public surface already equals a behavior spec.

title: TierZero HL↔CEX funding-arb playbook
key_finding: Maker-first/conditional-taker-hedge entry, 3–4× fee gate, 14d cap, margin keeper — desk is closed but the playbook is published; no artifact exists to reverse.

title: NeuralArb HL vs CEXs cost model
key_finding: Fee stack, slippage curve, child-order splitting, funding-snipe timing — closed desk, public cost model; alpha signal remains server-side and unrecoverable.

title: Tool inventory cross-reference: Ghidra/IDA/radare2-rizin/Frida/Wireshark/jadx/apktool/strings/binwalk/Burp
key_finding: Every artifact-RE tool is either unnecessary (no closed artifact with value) or contract-encumbered (venue clients) for these targets; own-traffic tools (mitmproxy/Wireshark) remain lawful for authorized sessions.
